_id: freq rung: ism24125_61250. LICENCE-EXEMPT band pair -- 24.125 GHz (ISM 24.00-24.25 GHz) paired with 61.25 GHz (ISM 61.0-61.5 GHz). Both carriers move, unlike freq001-008 which only ever shift L2 inside the protected GPS L-band. MEASURED CONSEQUENCES OF THE BAND CHOICE (computed, not assumed): first-order ionospheric delay scales as 1/f^2, so this pair sees 0.0007 x the L1 ionosphere on the high carrier and 0.0043 x on the low one; the ionosphere-free combination of this pair would amplify uncorrelated code noise by 1.198 x, against 2.975 x for GPS L1/L2 -- IF amplification follows FRACTIONAL separation, and this pair is 87.0% apart against L1/L2's 22.0%. Carrier wavelengths are 4.895 mm and 12.427 mm. SPECTRUM: 250 MHz and 500 MHz of allocation respectively. HELD FIXED ON PURPOSE: codeSigma0_m stays at the golden 0.30 / 0.45 m. A higher carrier does not by itself sharpen the code -- ranging noise follows chip rate and bandwidth, not carrier frequency -- so letting it fall with band would bake in the conclusion. This run is raw dual frequency with the golden's per-tower slant-iono state, i.e. the freq002 configuration with the band moved. CEILING RUNG, NOT A LINK-FEASIBLE DESIGN. 61.25 GHz sits inside the 60 GHz oxygen absorption complex, where sea-level specific attenuation is of order 10-15 dB/km. A GEO slant path through the whole atmosphere is not closeable there at any practical power. This rung answers 'how far does the ionosphere argument go' and nothing else. [SUPERSEDED 2026-08-11: this note used to end 'the simulation models the ionosphere and the wavelength, NOT the oxygen absorption, so its link margin is fiction.' The simulation CAN now model it -- see _linkClosure below for the computed figure and the resolve-time refusal. With cfg.atmosphere.gaseousAbsorption.enable = false, which is the default, the original sentence still describes what this rung runs, and any figure quoted from it must carry that exclusion.]
_linkClosure: REFUSED AT RESOLVE TIME WHENEVER ABSORPTION IS MODELLED. The _id note above says this rung's link margin is fiction; that is now a computed number rather than an assertion. ITU-R P.676-13 Annex 1, integrated over the P.835 mean annual global atmosphere, gives 161.47 dB of gaseous attenuation at ZENITH for 61.25 GHz. A nominal 45 dB-Hz link with 6 dB of zenith gain therefore reaches -110.5 dB-Hz, i.e. 135.5 dB short of a 25 dB-Hz tracking threshold in the BEST-CASE geometry -- straight up, no obliquity, no rain, no margin. ConfigFactory.finalizeConfig REFUSES this configuration outright when cfg.atmosphere.gaseousAbsorption.enable is true, rather than running a simulation that cannot produce a measurement. THE RUNG IS RETAINED ON PURPOSE, not deleted: with absorption off it still answers the only question it was built for -- how far the ionosphere argument goes -- and deleting it would discard a documented negative result. Any figure quoted from this rung must carry the exclusion, per the ch8 scope wording. Table and provenance: models.atmosphere.GaseousAbsorption; generator analysis/generate_gas_absorption_table.m.
